notes:
Account summary (evaluation):
- Arcadia building enterprise document search + “answer on top” product. Core flow: query -> embed -> vector retrieval (Pinecone) -> rerank top-K -> optional short answer/summarization.
- Primary interest: reducing inference spend on rerank + non-streaming summarization while keeping tail latency predictable.

Workload details / requirements (from calls + email notes):
- Workloads:
  - Embeddings: high volume (indexing + query-time). Query embeddings must be fast, indexing can be batch/offline.
  - Reranking: query-time, strict latency sensitivity. Typical rerank: 50–200 candidate passages.
  - Answer generation: lower volume; often non-streaming for “answer card”, sometimes streaming in internal analyst UI.
- Latency targets (verbatim-ish):
  - “Search has to feel instant.” Target end-to-end p95 for query-time AI portion < ~700–900ms.
  - Rerank p95 target < ~120–180ms; p99 must not exceed ~350ms during burst.
  - Embedding p95 target < ~80–150ms for query-time (indexing can be slower).
- Concurrency: bursty. They described weekday peaks with 10–30 concurrent queries per tenant; spikes when large customers roll out to new departments.
- Prompt length distribution:
  - Rerank inputs short-to-medium; answer generation prompts can be long when they attach multiple snippets.
  - They want guardrails for long-context requests to avoid queue blowups.
- Cost sensitivity:
  - Current baseline spend is “too spiky” with their mix of workloads; leadership wants a predictable per-query cost model.
  - Strong interest in Redwood’s cost-efficient tier if it can meet rerank tail-latency constraints; willing to use standard/fast tier selectively for interactive routes.

Batching tiers discussion (key takeaways):
- They asked how Redwood chooses fast vs standard vs cost-efficient by default and how they can pin a tier per route.
- They liked that tier defaults are explainable (Console “why this profile” + reason codes). Requested we share example reason codes that would show: override vs tier default vs overload/backpressure mode.
- They are open to:
  - cost-efficient tier for reranking IF p99 stays within their guardrails
  - standard tier for answer generation by default
  - fast tier only for a small subset of routes (internal “analyst” UI)

Security / compliance notes:
- Deployment: preference for VPC/private networking (hosted in their VPC or Dedicated with isolation). Not asking for on-prem.
- Data handling questions:
  - Security asked explicitly whether tier selection affects logging/retention. We clarified tiers change runtime scheduling/batching behavior only; no change to data retention policy. They still want it in writing for their review packet.
- Requirements: SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, retention controls (short log retention), US-only residency for initial rollout.

Activity timeline:
- 2026-01-08: Record created after inbound from Arcadia eng lead (doc-search scaling + rerank cost concerns).
- 2026-01-22: Technical deep dive (Fireflies) focused on latency vs cost tiers; they asked for p95/p99 tier targets + how overrides work.
- 2026-02-06: Follow-up email: requested POC plan and guidance on choosing tiers for reranking vs summarization.
- 2026-02-14: Shared draft customer-facing tier messaging + early benchmark summary (no commitments, just ranges).
- 2026-02-21: Internal sync: confirmed we can support route-level tier pinning + explainability; flagged need to keep metric cardinality bounded.

Open questions / risks logged by AE:
- Need to confirm their model preferences for reranking (they’re currently benchmarking Cohere Rerank; open to Redwood catalog options if quality is comparable).
- Need representative prompt set from Arcadia (they offered to provide 200–500 anonymized queries + doc snippets). Without this, perf results may not match prod.
- Procurement: deciding between Dedicated vs Hosted with usage caps; asked for estimated monthly cost at 1M / 5M / 10M queries.

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood: propose tier mapping per route (rerank: cost-efficient w/ guardrails; query embeddings: standard; indexing embeddings: cost-efficient).
- Arcadia: provide sample workload stats (prompt length distribution, candidate counts for rerank, concurrency peaks).
- Schedule security review checkpoint after we deliver written statement on tier/logging + draft architecture diagram for VPC connectivity.
